title: "Getting started with SkosmosR"
output: rmarkdown::html_vignette

  %\VignetteIndexEntry{Getting started with SkosmosR}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::rmarkdown}

`SkosmosR` is a provider-independent R client for the Skosmos REST API v1.
High-level JSON-returning functions return **tibbles**. Nested Skosmos objects
are retained as list-columns where flattening would lose information. RDF
functions return RDF text/raw data or an `rdflib` graph, and
`skosmos_request()` remains a low-level escape hatch that returns the original
JSON structure.

```{r setup, eval=FALSE}
library(SkosmosR)
```

## 1. Finto: basic workflow

```{r finto, eval=FALSE}
finto <- skosmos_client("https://api.finto.fi/rest/v1/")

skosmos_ping(finto)

vocabs <- skosmos_vocabularies(finto, lang = "en")
class(vocabs)
vocabs

skosmos_vocabulary(finto, "yso", lang = "en")

hits <- skosmos_search(
  finto,
  query = "forest",
  vocabs = "yso",
  lang = "en",
  maxhits = 10
)
hits

skosmos_vocabulary_search(
  finto,
  vocid = "yso",
  query = "forest",
  lang = "en",
  maxhits = 10
)

skosmos_lookup(finto, "yso", label = "cat", lang = "en")
skosmos_types(finto, lang = "en")
skosmos_top_concepts(finto, "yso", lang = "en")
skosmos_groups(finto, "yso", lang = "en")
skosmos_vocabulary_statistics(finto, "yso", lang = "en")
skosmos_label_statistics(finto, "yso", lang = "en")
skosmos_index_letters(finto, "yso", lang = "en")
skosmos_index(finto, "yso", letter = "A", lang = "en")
```

### Concept relationships

```{r finto-concept, eval=FALSE}
cosmology <- skosmos_concept(
  finto,
  vocid = "yso",
  uri = "http://www.yso.fi/onto/yso/p7160"
)

skosmos_label(cosmology, "en")
skosmos_broader(cosmology, "en")
skosmos_broader_transitive(cosmology, "en")
skosmos_narrower(cosmology, "en")
skosmos_narrower_transitive(cosmology, "en")
skosmos_related(cosmology, "en")
skosmos_children(cosmology, "en")
skosmos_hierarchy(cosmology, "en")
skosmos_mappings(cosmology, "en")
```

### RDF access

```{r finto-rdf, eval=FALSE}
skosmos_data(
  finto,
  uri = "http://www.yso.fi/onto/yso/p7160",
  vocid = "yso",
  format = "text/turtle"
)

skosmos_vocabulary_data(
  finto,
  vocid = "yso",
  format = "text/turtle"
)

skosmos_concept_data(
  cosmology,
  format = "application/ld+json"
)
```

## 2. Public Skosmos instances used as compatibility examples

`skosmos_instances()` contains a convenience registry. It is intentionally not
presented as an exhaustive worldwide census because Skosmos is self-hosted and
public installations can move or disappear.

```{r registry, eval=FALSE}
skosmos_instances()
skosmos_test_registry()
```

The same code pattern works for each installation:

```{r generic-pattern, eval=FALSE}
client <- skosmos_client("https://example.org/rest/v1/")
skosmos_vocabularies(client, lang = "en")
skosmos_search(client, query = "data", lang = "en", maxhits = 5)
```

### Finto — National Library of Finland

```{r example-finto, eval=FALSE}
client <- skosmos_client("https://api.finto.fi/rest/v1/")
skosmos_vocabularies(client, "en")
skosmos_vocabulary_search(client, "yso", "forest", lang = "en")
```

### UNESCO Vocabulary Services

```{r example-unesco, eval=FALSE}
client <- skosmos_client("https://vocabularies.unesco.org/rest/v1/")
v <- skosmos_vocabularies(client, "en")
v

# Use an ID returned by the server; on the UNESCO service the thesaurus is
# commonly exposed under the UNESCO vocabulary identifier.
skosmos_search(client, "education", lang = "en", maxhits = 10)
```

### FAO AGROVOC

```{r example-agrovoc, eval=FALSE}
client <- skosmos_client("https://agrovoc.fao.org/browse/rest/v1/")
skosmos_vocabularies(client, "en")
skosmos_search(client, "forest", lang = "en", maxhits = 10)

agrovoc_concept <- skosmos_concept(
  client,
  vocid = "agrovoc",
  uri = "http://aims.fao.org/aos/agrovoc/c_3077"
)
skosmos_label(agrovoc_concept, "en")
skosmos_broader(agrovoc_concept, "en")
```

### NFFA-Europe MetaRepo / PRIMA

```{r example-nffa, eval=FALSE}
client <- skosmos_client("https://metarepo.nffa.eu/skosmos/rest/v1/")
skosmos_vocabularies(client, "en")
skosmos_vocabulary(client, "prima", "en")
skosmos_vocabulary_search(client, "prima", "instrument", lang = "en")

instrument <- skosmos_concept(
  client,
  "prima",
  "https://purls.helmholtz-metadaten.de/skosmos/prima/instrument"
)
skosmos_broader(instrument, "en")
skosmos_narrower(instrument, "en")
```

### MET Norway Vocabulary Service

The Skosmos user interface is rooted at `https://vocab.met.no/`, while the
REST documentation is linked separately by the service. Do not infer the REST
path from its SPARQL path.

```{r example-metno, eval=FALSE}
client <- skosmos_client("https://vocab.met.no/rest/v1/")
skosmos_ping(client)
v <- skosmos_vocabularies(client, "en")
v

# Example vocabulary visible in the service:
skosmos_vocabulary(client, "CFSTDN", lang = "en")
skosmos_vocabulary_search(
  client,
  "CFSTDN",
  query = "air_temperature",
  lang = "en",
  maxhits = 10
)
```

### ILC4CLARIN / CNR

This is a particularly useful compatibility target because it exposes many
vocabularies. The following endpoint has been successfully exercised with
`skosmos_ping()` and `skosmos_vocabularies()`.

```{r example-ilc4clarin, eval=FALSE}
client <- skosmos_client(
  "https://vocabs.ilc4clarin.ilc.cnr.it/skosmos/rest/v1/"
)

vocabs <- skosmos_vocabularies(client, "en")
vocabs

# Select one vocabulary ID, not the whole vector.
vocid <- vocabs$id[1]
skosmos_vocabulary(client, vocid, "en")

skosmos_vocabulary(client, "agroterm", "en")
skosmos_vocabulary(client, "echoes_glossary", "en")
skosmos_vocabulary(client, "multilingual_architecture", "en")
```

To test every vocabulary returned by an installation:

```{r loop-vocabularies, eval=FALSE}
results <- lapply(vocabs$id, function(vocid) {
  tryCatch(
    {
      skosmos_vocabulary(client, vocid, "en")
      tibble::tibble(vocid = vocid, status = "PASS", error = NA_character_)
    },
    error = function(e) {
      tibble::tibble(
        vocid = vocid,
        status = "FAIL",
        error = conditionMessage(e)
      )
    }
  )
})

do.call(rbind, results)
```

### BARTOC Skosmos

BARTOC operates a Skosmos-based terminology service and exposes many
individual vocabularies. Because BARTOC vocabulary-facing URLs and deployment
paths may differ from a single canonical REST root, discover or confirm the
REST v1 endpoint for the selected BARTOC vocabulary before constructing the
client. Once confirmed, the usage is identical:

```{r example-bartoc, eval=FALSE}
bartoc <- skosmos_client("https://CONFIRMED-BARTOC-SKOSMOS/rest/v1/")
skosmos_vocabularies(bartoc, "en")
skosmos_search(bartoc, "education", lang = "en")
```

Examples discussed during package testing include BARTOC-hosted entries for
UNBIS, TheSoz, RBMS, ADMS and other controlled vocabularies. They are useful
additional vocabulary-level targets, but they should not be hard-coded as
independent API servers unless their REST root has been confirmed.

## 3. Complete Skosmos REST v1 coverage in SkosmosR

The high-level package interface covers the standard global, vocabulary and
concept operations discussed in the Skosmos REST v1 API.

### Global operations

```{r api-global, eval=FALSE}
skosmos_vocabularies(client)
skosmos_search(client, query = "term")
skosmos_label_uri(client, uri = "https://example.org/concept/1")
skosmos_types(client)
skosmos_data(client, uri = "https://example.org/concept/1")
```

### Vocabulary operations

```{r api-vocabulary, eval=FALSE}
skosmos_vocabulary(client, "vocid")
skosmos_types(client, vocid = "vocid")
skosmos_top_concepts(client, "vocid")
skosmos_vocabulary_data(client, "vocid")
skosmos_vocabulary_search(client, "vocid", "term")
skosmos_lookup(client, "vocid", "label")
skosmos_vocabulary_statistics(client, "vocid")
skosmos_label_statistics(client, "vocid")
skosmos_index_letters(client, "vocid")
skosmos_index(client, "vocid", "A")
skosmos_groups(client, "vocid")
skosmos_new_concepts(client, "vocid")
skosmos_modified_concepts(client, "vocid")
```

### Concept operations

```{r api-concept, eval=FALSE}
concept <- skosmos_concept(client, "vocid", "https://example.org/concept/1")

skosmos_concept_data(concept)
skosmos_label(concept)
skosmos_broader(concept)
skosmos_broader_transitive(concept)
skosmos_narrower(concept)
skosmos_narrower_transitive(concept)
skosmos_related(concept)
skosmos_children(concept)
skosmos_group_members(concept)
skosmos_hierarchy(concept)
skosmos_mappings(concept)
```

If a Skosmos installation has a deployment-specific extension not represented
by a high-level helper, use `skosmos_request()` without losing access to that
server functionality:

```{r low-level, eval=FALSE}
skosmos_request(
  client,
  path = "vocid/customRoute",
  query = list(lang = "en")
)
```

## 4. Tibbles and nested responses

High-level JSON methods return tibbles:

```{r tibbles, eval=FALSE}
x <- skosmos_vocabularies(finto, "en")
class(x)
# c("tbl_df", "tbl", "data.frame")
```

Simple arrays become one-column tibbles. Arrays of concepts become ordinary
multi-column tibbles. Nested JSON structures are retained as list-columns so
that hierarchy and mapping information is not discarded.

`skosmos_request()` intentionally returns the original parsed JSON object for
advanced users who need the exact server payload.

## 5. APIs discussed that are not Skosmos REST APIs

Not every vocabulary/data API is a Skosmos API. In particular,
`https://data.unesco.org/api/explore/v2.1/` is an Opendatasoft Explore API and
should not be used as a SkosmosR compatibility target. The OpenAIRE/Zenodo API
mapping publication discussed alongside this project is useful background on
terminology-service interoperability, but OpenAIRE itself is not a Skosmos
REST endpoint.
